short: GPT-2 correction of one ASR transcript is neither first nor near the field: LLM correction of silent-EMG hypotheses already reached 12.2% WER on this benchmark; here 30% on ~100 utterances, one run.
position: The paper changes the recognizer of EMG-synthesized speech (M06, standard) and adds GPT-2 correction of its single transcript (M07, behind). The claim to be the first LLM correction stage for silent speech does not hold: an earlier study passed beam lists and model ensembles from silent EMG on the same benchmark to an LLM and reached 12.2% test WER, against 30% here. The recognizer gain, 36% to 32.5%, swaps the scoring ASR on the same synthesized audio rather than improving the silent-speech system, and later work shows the scorer alone moves WER from 21.32% to 11.89%. Results come from one run on about 100 test utterances whose split is not identified, with no seeds, uncertainty or selection data for the 0.7 threshold.
